new_statements.rule_in_words: Khisa is described as a tone language (high vs. non-high marked; H-tone spreading; final-syllable H lowered to mid). Alongside tone, Miehe refers to a word stress located on the first syllable of disyllabic words (as in closely related Kaasa), whose phonetic correlate is strengthening/gemination of the following (stem-second or suffix) consonant. No fuller accent rule is given and the author calls the prosodic observations provisional.
new_statements.exceptions: Stress-triggered consonant lengthening 'may evidently be blocked (or compensated?) by glottalisation' in one speaker's (Kolokobo's) speech (p.152); tonal observations explicitly provisional.
new_statements.domain_note: Statements concern citation-form nouns (disyllabic words, noun stem + class suffix); stress is mentioned only as a conditioning factor for consonant strengthening, not as a worked-out accentual system. Access was via Google Books snippets only; full pages 146-147 and 152 not seen.
new_statements.identity_note: Miehe 2007 describes Khisa [Khìsà] as spoken in and around Mangodara, Comoé Province, Burkina Faso (speakers Ouattara Kolokobo of Farakoroso, Ouattara Adulai of Mangodara, etc.), i.e. khis1238 proper; ethnonym Komono, people Khıpa. Coulibaly et al. 2022 describe 'Kepar', the Komono variety of Bolé (Bounkani region, NE Côte d'Ivoire), which Glottolog also files under khis1238 [kqm]. Ouattara 1991/2002 title the language 'dogosé-khisé' / 'dògòsè variété klámáàsísè' — Glottolog assigns these to kqm, but the naming overlaps with Dogosé [dos] (dogo1295), so identity should be checked if those works are obtained.

tone_statements.citation: Coulibaly, Tidiane. 2023. Les modalités dérivationnelles verbales du kepar, parler komono : langue gur de Côte d’Ivoire. Akofena, Hors-série n°04 (Actes de la 2ème e-journée 2023, juin 2023), 71-82. Abidjan: CRAC-INSAAC / L3DL-CI, Université Félix Houphouët-Boigny.
tone_statements.quote: [p.78, §3.1] La réalisation ici de [-me] dépend du ton de la voyelle de la structure CV de base. - Si le ton de la voyelle de base est haut alors on aura ̸ mé/. hú « Accoucher » húmé « mourir ». - Si le ton de la voyelle de base est bas alors on aura / mè /. (b) sì « Défendre » sìmè « chavirer ». ... [p.73 fn.3] Nous avons omis le ton car comme on le verra à la suite, pour passer du nom à l’acteur ou du verbe à l’acteur, tous les monèmes créent une harmonie tonale avec –dàrjà. Dans cet exemple précis, la base est « sɔ́ ̃ », c’est –dàrjà (qualificatif de l’acteur) qui vient la transformée en « sɔ̀ ̃ » car il lui impose son ton bas.
tone_statements.translation: [p.78] The realisation of [-me] here depends on the tone of the vowel of the base CV structure. If the tone of the base vowel is high, we get /mé/: hú 'give birth', húmé 'die'. If the tone of the base vowel is low, we get /mè/: sì 'forbid', sìmè 'capsize'. ... [p.73 fn.3] We have left out tone because, as will be seen below, in passing from noun to agent or from verb to agent all the monemes form a tonal harmony with -dàrjà. In this precise example the base is sɔ́̃; it is -dàrjà (agent qualifier) that turns it into sɔ̀̃, because it imposes its low tone on it.
tone_statements.locator: §3.1 'La formation par suffixation de /-mE/ à la base CV', p.78, schema top of p.79; footnote 3, p.73

sources.note: Not a tone study, but first-hand tone-marked Kepar data with an explicit two-height tone opposition used in the analysis: derivational suffixes /-mE/ and /-mã/ surface with high tone [-mé], [-má̰] after a high-toned CV base and low tone [-mè], [-mà̰] after a low-toned base (§3.1-3.2, p.78-79); fn.3 p.73 describes 'harmonie tonale' whereby agentive -dàrjà imposes its low tone on the base (sɔ́ ̃ -> sɔ̀ ̃). Consistent with the H vs non-H two-tone statement listed here (Miehe 2007); no inventory statement, no stress statement.
